title: The Gallery After Hours
brief: A small painting is reported missing after a private viewing. Three staff members offer different accounts of the final twenty minutes. Your task is to test the records before settling on a theory.

clues.title: Visitor log
clues.body: The final visitor signed out at 8:42 PM. The east corridor access log records a door opening at 8:51 PM.

clues.title: Conservation note
clues.body: A conservator recorded that the painting was removed from its frame for inspection earlier that afternoon and rehung before the viewing.

clues.title: Camera gap
clues.body: The corridor camera shows an empty front desk for six minutes. The recording does not show who entered the storage room.

clues.title: Key register
clues.body: The east corridor master key was checked out by facilities and returned at 9:03 PM.

question: What is the most defensible next investigative step?
options: Assume the last visitor stole it
Reconcile the key register, access log and camera gap
Accuse the guard because the desk was empty
explanation: Reconcile independent access records and establish who could enter during the relevant window. A camera gap or proximity alone is not proof of guilt.

title: The Riverside Notebook
brief: A research notebook disappears after a storm. A badge log, paper fragment and delivery receipt appear to point in different directions.

clues.title: Weather report
clues.body: Heavy rain began at 6:10 PM and continued until 7:25 PM.

clues.title: Building access
clues.body: The side entrance registered a badge entry at 6:48 PM, but the badge holder says the card was misplaced that day.

clues.title: Paper fragment
clues.body: A fragment near the loading area matches the notebook's paper stock, but that stock is used throughout the building.

clues.title: Delivery receipt
clues.body: A courier signed for a package at the main entrance at 7:02 PM. The receipt is time-stamped by the front desk system.

question: What can the evidence support right now?
options: The badge holder definitely took the notebook
The paper fragment proves where it went
The evidence narrows a window but does not identify a person
explanation: The records provide leads, not proof. The badge event needs corroboration and the paper stock is not unique.

title: The Darkroom Negative
brief: An archive's original photographic negative is missing. A digital scan exists, but its metadata conflicts with the accession book.

clues.title: Accession book
clues.body: The negative was checked into drawer 4B on Monday. The entry is written in a different ink from adjacent entries.

clues.title: Scanner metadata
clues.body: The scan file was created on Tuesday, but the workstation clock was found to be six hours fast during a later audit.

clues.title: Glove residue
clues.body: A glove was found near the cabinet. The archive uses the same glove type for routine handling.

clues.title: Staff rota
clues.body: Two staff members had authorised access to the darkroom that week; the rota does not record exact entry times.

question: Which conclusion is justified?
options: The ink proves the accession entry was forged
The metadata gives the exact removal time
The current evidence is insufficient; preserve originals and reconcile time sources
explanation: Ink difference, device-clock drift and common gloves are limitations, not proof. Preserve the original files and documents, then corroborate timestamps independently.
